run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: Investigation of reported database connection timeouts for the blue-whale app in namespace app-94. I ran the approved runbook database-troubleshooting: (1) application status — the blue-whale Deployment in app-94 has 1/1 ready/available replicas and its pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-tlnx7 is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, created 2026-11-22T09:08:10Z with only Normal events (Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started, SuccessfulCreate, ScalingReplicaSet 'from 0 to 1'); (2) application logs — fetch_pod_logs for blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-tlnx7 returned zero lines (view status no_data, so it cannot support a fact; no previous container instance); (3) database Service/Endpoints — Service postgres exists in app-94 (ClusterIP 10.96.89.164, port 5432, selector app=postgres-db) while its Endpoints object has no subsets, and it is the only Endpoints object in the whole cluster without subsets; (4) connectivity test from the app pod — could not be carried out, no exec/network tool was available; (5) database health — could not be checked because no Postgres pod, Deployment or StatefulSet exists anywhere in the cluster (25 Deployments, 1 StatefulSet = alertmanager in otel-demo, 33 pods, none labelled app=postgres-db); (6) connection-pool configuration — read from the Deployment: DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20. So the DB hostname the app uses resolves to a Service with no backing endpoint at all, which is the strongest evidenced explanation for failed DB connections; however no blue-whale-side error, latency or failure record could be observed because the Prometheus and Jaeger sources were unavailable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) in this Run and the pod wrote no log lines, so the reported timeouts are not directly confirmed in telemetry. Conclusion is partial.

claims.text: The Deployment blue-whale in namespace app-94 reports replicas=1 with readyReplicas=1 and availableReplicas=1, and its pod is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-tlnx7 (owner ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5), phase Running, container ready=true, restartCount=0, started 2026-11-22T09:08:10Z.

The blue-whale container spec in app-94 runs image python:3.9-slim with command python /app/app.py (code mounted from secret blue-whale-app) and environment DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20; no ports or probes are declared.

Service postgres in namespace app-94 is a ClusterIP service (clusterIP 10.96.89.164) exposing TCP port 5432 with selector app=postgres-db; its Endpoints object has subsets=null, i.e. no backing addresses.

Of the 31 Endpoints objects in the cluster, postgres in namespace app-94 is the only one with an empty subsets list, while the blue-whale Endpoints in app-94 does resolve to pod IP 10.244.0.29 of blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-tlnx7 on port 8080.

No Postgres workload exists in the cluster: of 25 Deployments cluster-wide only blue-whale is in app-94 and none is a postgres/database workload, the only StatefulSet is alertmanager in otel-demo, and none of the 33 pods carries label app=postgres-db or a postgres name.

Namespace app-94 was created 2026-11-22T09:08:09Z and ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 was created 2026-11-22T09:08:10Z; the events for that moment are the Deployment event 'Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1', a ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate event, and Normal Pod events Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started — all at 2026-11-22T09:08:10Z, about 38 seconds before the authorized window ended.

Namespace app-94 contains exactly one ConfigMap, kube-root-ca.crt; no application or fault-injection ConfigMap (for example one carrying error/delay/failure settings for blue-whale or its database) was observed in that namespace.

The blue-whale pod itself shows no crash or restart symptom: container ready=true, restartCount=0, lastState empty, and pod conditions Ready and ContainersReady both True; so a container crash or restart loop is not what the observed state shows.

The leading explanation for blue-whale's database connection timeouts is that its configured database endpoint postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 maps to Service postgres in app-94, which has zero endpoints (no pod carries app=postgres-db, and no Postgres workload exists in the cluster), so every connection attempt to that ClusterIP cannot reach a server and fails or hangs until DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30 seconds expires.

A second, not excluded possibility is a provisioning gap rather than a selector mismatch: namespace app-94 was created at 2026-11-22T09:08:09Z, so blue-whale was deployed into a namespace without a database and the Postgres workload and credentials were never created there; on that reading the empty Endpoints are a symptom of the missing database rather than the cause of it.

Provide the database the Service postgres in app-94 expects: deploy a Postgres workload whose pods carry label app=postgres-db in namespace app-94 (or correct the Service selector to the actual database pod labels), then confirm the Endpoints object postgres in app-94 gains a 5432 address before re-testing blue-whale's DB connection.

After the database is reachable, verify the app-side signals this Run could not read (Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable): blue-whale request and DB error rate plus connection-attempt latency, and whether DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30 and DB_POOL_SIZE=20 in the Deployment blue-whale env remain appropriate for the real database latency.

gaps: blue-whale's own failure evidence could not be observed: fetch_pod_logs for blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-tlnx7 returned zero lines (view 8b0ff865-2643-45d2-b1f1-5778fea726c0-t0:0993540f-6ffd-427a-a210-2b972b6a864a has status no_data; no previous container instance), so no connection-timeout or error line from the application was available.

Prometheus was unavailable throughout this Run (metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no metric series such as kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="app-94"}, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total or service-level latency/error metrics could be checked for blue-whale; its error rate and latency are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable as well (traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) and the traces_search call for service blue-whale was rejected as INVALID_PARAMS, so no trace evidence of blue-whale database calls exists in this Run.

NetworkPolicy and ResourceQuota queries returned empty results with view status no_data (bdf0ad99-f950-42ce-8a18-b2f04b3323b9-t1:2e29659e-5e07-4be4-98bc-1b9d30b8a7de, 10e1aa0d-a8e0-450b-9e02-8588a9447d04-t2:d94c4137-8d93-44cd-95bf-881f7a5352d6), so I cannot state from citable evidence whether egress from app-94 is restricted; the runbook's connectivity test from inside the blue-whale pod and any direct database health check could not be executed because no exec/database tool is available and no Postgres pod exists.

The application code and DB credentials live in secret blue-whale-app, which cannot be read, so what the app actually attempts (host resolution, retry logic, timeout enforcement) could not be verified.

Whether a Postgres database ever existed in app-94 (for example one deleted before 09:08:10Z) is unknown: the pod, Endpoints and Deployment views are the cluster's state at query time, no deletion or eviction events appeared in the window, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
next_steps: Deploy or restore the Postgres database for namespace app-94 with pod label app=postgres-db matching Service postgres port 5432, or point the Service selector at the real database pods, and verify Endpoints postgres in app-94 is populated.
Once endpoints exist, re-run the runbook's connectivity check from the blue-whale pod (nc -zv postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local 5432) and read the app logs for connection attempts.
Restore or check the Prometheus and Jaeger observability sources so blue-whale's DB error rate and connection latency can be measured instead of inferred.
Confirm with platform owners what caused the missing database (intentional teardown, failed provisioning, or a database outside this cluster), since change_history is not integrated in this Run.
